title: Department of War Daily Briefing
description: Secretary-level initiatives, acquisition, Golden Dome, operations and policy across the Department of War.
readFirst: Covers Nov. 3–10. New: the Department of War said Nov. 9 that Secretary Hegseth directed an overhaul of professional military education, including warfighter chairs, end-of-course wargames and exams, and an end to lifetime tenure for newly hired civilian faculty. The Office of Strategic Capital's Rocket Lab loan is on the tech page. No war.gov daily contracts release for Nov. 9 or Nov. 10 could be opened. No new Army or Department of War enterprise software agreement was found. The Nov. 2 DoDEA vacancy note aged out.

items.headline: Hegseth directs senior military colleges to drop tenure and grade warfighting exams
items.summary: The Department of War said Nov. 9 that Secretary Pete Hegseth directed an overhaul of professional military education across senior service colleges and intermediate-level education. The release says the department will judge programs by whether they forge leaders who will win America's wars, and that the plan creates Warfighter Chair positions for O-5 and O-6 commanders fresh from operational deployments. It says subjective seminar grading will be replaced with standardized end-of-course wargames and comprehensive exams, and that newly hired civilian faculty will no longer receive lifetime tenure or emeritus status, moving instead to three-year performance-based contracts. The Under Secretary of War for Personnel and Readiness is directed to track the requirements.

items.headline: Hegseth's post-election video calls for a $1.5 trillion defense budget
items.summary: Federal News Network reported Nov. 5 that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth posted a video Thursday, filmed on the steps of the Pentagon's ceremonial entrance, defending the Iran war as a courageous and historic effort that will ensure Iran never gets a nuclear weapon. Hegseth called on every patriotic member of Congress to vote for a $1.5 trillion defense budget and said Rep. Thomas Massie's eight articles of impeachment are a sham. Federal News Network said the video is his first public statement on Tuesday's midterm results, that Democrats will retake both chambers, and that Massie plans to refile the articles when lawmakers return next week. It said Trump has publicly defended Hegseth while reportedly mulling whether to oust him, and that Hegseth's name has been floated for the Senate seat Tennessee Governor-elect Marsha Blackburn will vacate in January.

items.headline: Trump tells reporters Hegseth is staying after the midterm losses
items.summary: ABC News reported Nov. 4 that President Donald Trump said Wednesday that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth would remain on the job and told reporters he was doing a great job, while acknowledging that the war with Iran had contributed to Republicans' midterm losses. Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell told ABC News that Hegseth is 100 percent committed to leading the department until the end of President Trump's term and will not be deterred by what Parnell called phony investigations. ABC News said Democrats are preparing to use their new congressional majority to scrutinize the Pentagon, with Hegseth expected to be a target for possible impeachment, including the Iran war, strikes on suspected drug-smuggling boats, and firings of senior officers. ABC News said Vice President JD Vance wrote that the reason Republicans lost is the war, and that its voter poll found 34 percent of U.S. House voters called the Iran war crucial to their vote.

items.headline: Federal News Network: DIA is asking industry about a classified analysis vehicle near $17 billion
items.summary: Federal News Network's Nov. 6 newscast said the Defense Intelligence Agency is starting the next version of its Solutions for Intelligence Analysis multiple-award vehicle, SIA 4. The outlet said a request for information would make SIA 4 a classified contract, so vendors would need an active Top Secret facility clearance. It said the vehicle would have a five-year base and a five-year option, with a total ceiling of about $17 billion. Responses are due Nov. 24, and the agency expects an industry event in early 2027.

items.headline: Office of Strategic Capital commits conditional loans to 6K and Halo Industries
items.summary: The Department of War said Nov. 5 that the Office of Strategic Capital signed a $250 million conditional loan commitment with 6K, Inc. to scale nickel-manganese-cobalt cathode production at its PlusCAM facility in Jackson, Tennessee, matched by an additional $250 million in private capital. The release says the material is for defense platforms, uncrewed aerial systems, tactical communications, and energy infrastructure, that the United States produces less than 1 percent of its NMC cathode needs domestically, and that financial close still requires further diligence. The same day the office signed a $75 million conditional loan commitment with Halo Industries to scale laser slicing of silicon-carbide wafers in Santa Clara, California, crowding in an additional $75 million for uses including radar, electronic warfare, hypersonics, and directed energy. Both releases say the commitments are not yet a financial close, and Under Secretary for Research and Engineering Emil Michael endorsed each one.

items.headline: JIATF-401 awards CHAOS 1 more than $6.9 million for CENTCOM counter-drone radar
items.summary: The Department of War said Nov. 4 that Joint Interagency Task Force 401 awarded CHAOS 1, Inc. a contract valued at more than $6.9 million for Vanquish Prime radar systems to strengthen counter-unmanned aircraft defense in the U.S. Central Command area. The release says the radars provide long-range detection and tracking, and that the award includes training and technology for integration. Lt. Col. Matthew Strohman, the task force's capability manager for mobile counter-UAS, said the threat from unmanned systems is evolving and that the systems are meant to give forces in CENTCOM a detection layer. The release says the radars will go to designated locations in that area of responsibility.

items.headline: Watchdogs sued to shut down Hegseth's Project Meridian future-of-warfare panel
items.summary: Military.com reported Nov. 3 that Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington, Public Citizen, and the Project On Government Oversight sued in federal court in Washington to shut down Project Meridian, naming the department, Secretary Pete Hegseth, and Undersecretary for Research and Engineering Emil Michael. The complaint says the panel violates the Federal Advisory Committee Act, and Military.com said it counts 19 of 21 people involved as private-sector figures. Military.com said Hegseth commissioned the study in a Sept. 30 memo, told Michael to run it through a partner organization, and set findings for Jan. 28, 2027. A MITRE spokesperson told Military.com the Department of War contracted with MITRE's National Security Engineering Center to conduct the study, and a Pentagon spokesperson said the department does not comment on pending legislation.

items.headline: Department says DRPM-UxS fielded more than 24,000 counter-drone systems to CENTCOM
items.summary: The Department of War said Nov. 4 that the Direct Reporting Portfolio Manager for Unmanned Systems fielded, through about $782 million this year, more than 1,300 one-way-attack unmanned aerial vehicles, more than 100 unmanned surface and undersea vessels, and more than 24,000 counter-unmanned aerial systems to U.S. Central Command. The release says the counter-drone systems went out through Joint Interagency Task Force 401. Owen West, who the release calls CEO of Project Agincourt and DRPM-UxS, said the office was set up to put lethal technology in the hands of frontline troops and that the goal is to scale the capabilities across the joint force. The release says the effort is the operational foundation for Autonomous Warfare Command, a planned four-star command scheduled to stand up by Oct. 1, 2027, and that fielding will expand to Pacific Command, European Command, and the broader joint force.

items.headline: Air Force asks industry for more than 1,000 Extended Range Attack Munitions for Ukraine
items.summary: Defense News reported Nov. 3 that the U.S. Air Force is asking industry whether it can deliver a cruise missile intended for Ukraine, the Extended Range Attack Munition. The outlet said the request for information, due Nov. 19, describes a 500-pound-class air-launched weapon with a range greater than 250 nautical miles, a speed above Mach 0.6, and terminal accuracy within 10 meters even with degraded GPS. Defense News said companies should begin delivering the first of more than 1,000 missiles no later than three months after award, and finish within 15 months. It said the Air Force in 2024 awarded prototype work to Zone 5 Technologies and CoAspire, and conducted a live-warhead test at Eglin Air Force Base in January 2026.

items.headline: Space Force awards Viasat up to $450 million for a Golden Dome data-network operations center
items.summary: Breaking Defense reported Nov. 6 that the Space Force, in partnership with the Pentagon's Golden Dome office, awarded Viasat an indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract with a $450 million ceiling to design, field, and scale a Mission Operations Center for the Space Data Network Backbone. DefenseScoop reported the same day that the initial task order is valued at $115 million, and that the Pentagon earlier awarded SpaceX a $2.3 billion contract for a fully operational prototype of the low-Earth-orbit backbone by the end of 2027. Breaking Defense said Space Systems Command described the center as the central network orchestration hub for that backbone. DefenseScoop quoted Lt. Col. Alexa Eggert, materiel leader for the program, saying the center is a crucial step in maturing the network into a fully operational, multi-vendor capability.
